This is a sample G Code file for true 4 axis mode. Offsets and power modes are contained within the program in the header, followed by QAIC and SFCC parameters. Next the heights of the top and bottom of the part are set TP+TN, then it's essentially just pairs of coordinated for top and bottom head, with the first line of coordinates from each section containing a H and C value, each relating their relivant offset and power settings stated in the header. 
I can upload a more simple program if it helps.

Triage (maintainer, 2026-11-12: EDM is open for work): `P1`, `area:post`. This builds on the wire EDM slice from #290: the machine kind (#530, PR #551), the condition table (#531, PR #560), the 2-axis contour (#532) and the generic wire post (#533), which carries the codes as machine data - a Sodick dialect is then a machine file plus whatever the LN control needs beyond that. It is picked for code once #533 is in.

Note (UMA, mkinney fork): #533's generic wire post is now up as draft PR #1139 (codes as machine data, on #1123), so #617 can stack on it. UMA didn't pick #617 because its dialect source, the Sodick LN1W/LN2W training manual cited above, isn't on UMA's machine, and the dialect shouldn't be guessed. Whoever holds a copy is the right picker. The user-posted NC example above wasn't read (its generating CAM is unknown; clean room).
Do you need an example copy of the machine conditions table? Theres going to need to be custom importer for each of the main brands of control.

@spikeypineapple - yes please, that would unblock this. Plan (SKULL, mkinney fork): the Sodick dialect builds on the generic wire post in PR #1139 (#533, "codes as machine data"), so most of what makes a Sodick program a Sodick program can live in the machine file's `edm` section rather than in new post code. To get it right without guessing, it would help to have, from your own machine:

1. **The controller model** (and software version if you know it).
2. **One or two short programs you run today**, ideally a simple die (closed contour with a start hole) and, if you use them, one with skim passes. Plain text is fine. Please strip anything proprietary; we only need the structure: how a program starts and ends, how a condition is selected, how the wire offset/compensation is switched on and off and on which side, AWT thread/cut words, and the word for a pause/stop.
3. **A sample of the condition table** as you use it (the columns you set per condition: e.g. condition number, wire diameter, offset/gap, and anything else), so the importer/machine-file mapping matches real data.
4. Anything your post or the control requires that a generic ISO wire program would not have.

We won't copy any vendor post-processor text; the dialect is written from your examples and public RS-274 conventions, and you'd test the output on the machine before anyone relies on it. Once #1139 lands (it waits on #1123), this becomes a dialect on top of it.

Status (issue-worker-max, 2026-11-13): not claimed, no code written. This issue is waiting on input, and the dialect is not being guessed.

**What is in place on main now.** The foundation the earlier comments waited for has landed: the generic ISO wire post (`assets/posts/wire-iso.cps`, PR #1139), wire verify and the wire gouge law (#1144), taper (#1163) and tabs (#1158). A Sodick post can be built as a dialect on those seams as soon as its codes have a source.

**What is still missing.** The request of 2026-11-12 (controller model, sample programs, condition table sample) has no reply yet. Still needed from the machine owner:

1. The controller model and software version, stated (the sample's file name suggests an AQ600L; the control is not named).
2. One simple 2-axis program as run on the machine today: a closed die contour with a start hole, one rough pass, and if used one with skim passes. The sample above is a 4-axis taper program only.
3. A sample of the condition table as used (the columns per condition), and how offsets (H) are set.
4. For each word the post would have to write, what the control's own manual says it does. From the sample these are, as words to confirm and not as meanings assumed here: the header rows `C000 = ...` and `H000 = ...`, `QAIC(...)`, `SFCC...`, `TP` / `TN`, `G29`, `G74` / `G75`, `G149 G249 G348 ...`, `FLAG7`, `T84` / `T85` / `T87` / `T90` / `T91` / `T94`, `M03`, `M35`, and the program end.

**Source question for the maintainer.** Two things need a decision before code:

- The dialect source named in the first comment (Sodick *Wire EDM Training - Machine Operation, LN1W / LN2W Control*, part number 6300015) is held by one contributor and is not on this machine. A search today found no official, freely published Sodick programming reference for the LN control: only third-party code lists and document-sharing uploads, which cannot be checked against the control. A wrong code on a real machine is the worst outcome, so none of those was used.
- The sample program above was written by another CAM system's post (its header says so). Is the machine owner's own program an allowed clean-room source for the *control's* dialect, with each word confirmed against the control manual, or must the dialect come from the manual alone?

**What unblocks it.** Either the manual's programming pages are available to whoever picks this (then the post is written from them, with the sample used only as a test of the result), or the items 1-4 above arrive here and the maintainer allows them as the source. With neither, the honest result today would be a post that refuses almost every Sodick-specific feature by name, which is the generic `wire-iso.cps` already on main.

Nothing ran on a Sodick control. Labels are unchanged; the issue is free.
